name: Little Architect: Build or Burn
description: Marketed to children aged 5-10, Little Architect is a colorful tile-placement game in which players construct a vertical city — but resource cards are distributed wildly unequally at the start, and players who run out of 'permit tokens' see their structures legally demolished by a smiling cardboard 'Inspector' figure. The game's bright primary-color aesthetic masks mechanics that functionally teach tier-stratified resource scarcity: children who draw 'Shelf Start' cards begin with one-fifth the resources of 'Spire Start' players, and the rulebook frames this as 'exciting challenge mode.' Produced by Vantablack Immersive Children's Division under a HelixCorp education initiative.
story_hooks: Someone has been slipping altered rulebook inserts into retail copies that replace the 'exciting challenge mode' framing with blunt descriptions of how tier stratification actually works.

A Tier 1 child who has memorized every rule finds a genuine loophole that allows a Shelf Start player to win consistently — and a Tier 4 parent files a formal complaint demanding the game be 'rebalanced.'
A game designer who worked on Little Architect wants to blow the whistle on the intentional psychological mechanics but fears losing their HelixCorp contract and housing subsidy.
